title: Why This Is Kelly's Favorite Tattoo - NewsBreak
text:
By Tommy McNeill ,
4 hours ago
Over half of us on the show have tattoos. Free Beer was recently anointed with a massive octopus on his shoulder. Maitlynn has some new sparkles on her arms . But no one has more tattoos on the show than Kelly Cheese, who has been rocking a sleeve on her arm for years. It’s been part of her identity with the show for years.
READ MORE
But it may be a surprise to hear that Kelly’s most iconic tattoos are a relatively recent addition, a quest that really took off when she got her third tattoo. This third tattoo is not only her most intricate, but is also a) the base for her sleeve and b) her tattoo with the most meaning.
FBHW Kelly’s Sleeve Base “This is my third tattoo, I got it in 2022. But it’s my favorite because it was the beginning of my sleeve. The stack of books is obvious, because I love to read, but the florals are Golden Rods and Trilliums. Both can be used for traditional medicine. The bee is a nod to my Nanny and Papa, who were big gardeners, and my Papa kept bees.”
Goldenrod – In traditional medicine, women have used goldenrod, or Solidago species, to address conditions such as urinary tract infections (UTIs), yeast overgrowth, and inflammation related to menopause and postpartum recovery. The plant’s Latin name, Solidago, means “to make whole,” reflecting its long history as a healing herb.
Trilliums – used for gynecological issues, wound care, and as astringents. Common applications included inducing labor, stopping bleeding, treating boils, and eye ailments. However, wild harvesting is discouraged due to the trillium’s endangered status and fragile habitat.

Heck yes they do! From delicate, tastefully-concealed designs to full-on job-stoppers (that means ink on your hands or face!), country stars have it all. Scroll through this list to see 26 of the most amazing, meaningful and recognizable country music tattoos. Gallery Credit: Carena Liptak Facebook Brantley Gilbert's Statement of Support for the 2nd Amendment Plenty of people wear their beliefs on their sleeves, but Brantley Gilbert wears his support for the Second Amendment across his entire back. After he got the ink done in 2015, he posted a photo on Facebook so all his fans could admire his massive new design. Danielle Del Valle, Getty Images Brett Young's Wise Words The "In Case You Didn't Know" star has several tattoos, but if you ask us, his most eye-catching is the line of text running down his right forearm: "If it feels like home, follow its path."
Back in 2017, Young told Taste of Country that that phrase was paraphrased from poet R.M. Drake, and that it's his little reminder to stay true to what's right for him — even if the path ahead is daunting. Granger Smith's Tribute to His Late Son This tattoo commemorates Granger Smith's son River, who died in an accidental drowning at just three years old. Smith and his wife Amber have found a number of different ways to keep River's spirit alive, from making life-saving organ donations to raising awareness about water safety for parents everywhere. But Smith also designed to permanently etch River's name down his arm in a beautiful tribute to his child. Kevin Winter, Getty Images Blake Shelton's Questionable Deer Tracks Shelton'll be the first to make fun of his tattoo, which he says is the "crappiest" in country music — or maybe the world.
There's a hilarious story behind this ink: Shelton is an avid hunter and outdoorsman, so he thought a line of deer tracks would make an appropriate tattoo. But he drew the design for the tattoo himself, and, well — he might be known for his singing, but he's not known for his artwork. Most people mistook the tracks for lady bugs, even after he went back to the tattoo parlor and got barbed wire added to make his ink more manly.
Fortunately, Shelton's wife Gwen Stefani likes his ink, and isn't that what really matters? Stefani's 2023 single, "True Babe," features the line " Your tattoo still looks cute to me ." Meghan Patrick's "If You Know, You Know" Touring Tattoo Any traveling musician can relate to this one. Patrick's tattoo reads "my guitar fits in the overhead," and her bandmate Lenny Pey has a matching one on his wrist. We can only imagine how many times flight attendants have asked Patrick to gate-check her instrument. Gareth Cattermole,Getty Images Dolly Parton's Hidden Body Art Yep, Dolly Parton has a few tattoos, but you're about as likely to run into Bigfoot in the wild as you are to see them on display.
Parton says she got the tattoos to cover up keloid scarring from surgeries, and are mostly "pastel butterflies or little things, just to cover scars." She keeps them covered up when she's in public. Jason Kempin, Getty Images Jason Aldean's Florida Palm Trees Aldean got this tattoo from the Season 9 winner of Ink Master , Bubba Irwin! But the star factor isn't the only thing that makes these palm trees special: They wrap around Aldean's arm, looping in with an existing tattoo that bears the names of his three daughters (his son Memphis is represented on his other arm). The tattoo artist made a house call to give Aldean this ink, so that he could safely get tattooed without going out in public during the COVID-19 pandemic. Jason Kempin, Getty Images Garth Brooks' Mystery Tattoo Nobody knows quite what Brooks has got hidden up his sleeve — literally. Brooks got his first tattoo last year to celebrate his long-awaited Croke Park stadium shows in Ireland, and he has yet to reveal the ink publicly. He has said that his new tattoo is quite large — a full sleeve that extends onto his chest and back — and that it's a tribute to his daughters and his wife, Trisha Yearwood. Jason Kempin, Getty Images Carly Pearce's Meaningful Feather Pearce has a few tattoos, and they're all meaningful — they represent her love of country music, her home state and more. But nothing's sweeter than the delicate feather she got in inked in memory of her grandfather. In a social media post, Pearce explains that she decided on a feather after she kept finding red feathers in her home a few months after he died. Jesse Grant, Getty Images Ashley McBryde's Golden Gramophone McBryde added this piece of ink to her collection in early 2023 after winning her very first Grammy Award. The singer chose to get her golden gramophone done in American Traditional style, which fits with the rest of the tattoos already decorating her body. Rick Diamond, Getty Images Aaron Lewis' Cool-as-Heck Job-Stopper There's two kinds of tattooed people: Those who've got hands, face and neck tattoos, and those who don't. Aaron Lewis proved his dedication to his ink with a massive tattoo across his throat that reads "Don't Tread on Me." Carrie Underwood's Family Ink Carrie Underwood had a few tattoos already when she got this delicate heart inked on her foot in 2023, but what could be more meaningful than a matching design with your mom and sisters? That's exactly what the singer did to commemorate her Reflection Las Vegas residency. It marked her mom's first tattoo, and she and Underwood's two older sisters got their hearts on their wrists, while the singer herself opted to put it on the top of her right foot. YouTube Jason Aldean + Luke Bryan's Matching Ink Both official "Buckmen" — aka part-owners of the Buck Commander hunting franchise — Luke Bryan and Jason Aldean took their support of the brand to the next level when they both got the logo inked on their arms at the same time. That means they now officially have matching tattoos, though after they got inked, Aldean clarified that all the Buck Commander owners have the same design. Getty Images Jelly Roll's Quokka Jelly Roll's got tons of tattoos — maybe more than any other country artist — but one of our favorites is the quokka on his wrist. What's a quokka, you ask? It's a small, friendly Australian marsupial known for being friendly to humans and even obliging when people want to take selfies with them. Like koalas, quokkas eat eucalyptus leaves, which have a reputation for having psychotropic properties — though that's a myth, stemming from the fact that eucalyptus is very fibrous and animals who eat it need to sleep a lot to digest the leaves.
Still, the quokka's carefree personality makes it a role model to Jelly, who's known to enjoy indulging in some intoxicating substances himself. "Anytime I get upset in life, I look down at my wrist and I think, 'Just be a quokka. High and happy,'" he said when he explained his tattoo . Theo Wargo, Getty Images Keith Urban's Incredible Tribal Art Urban's got several tattoos that show a flair for tribal art, from the ultra-recognizable sun tattoo often peeking out of his shirts to the phoenix inscribed on his forearm to the intricate heart design around the name "Nicole" — that's his wife Nicole Kidman, of course — on his bicep. Ethan Miller, Getty Images Miranda Lambert's Signature Winged Pistol Lambert's had this forearm piece — two crossed pistols, flanked with wings — for most of her career. She got it while on tour with George Strait when she was 22, and according to The Boot, it caused some controversy in her family. "It's the first thing I ever did without asking my parents," Lambert said once. "My dad didn't speak to me for a week." Twitter Jason Isbell's Sobriety Tally Jason Isbell has been open about his experience with alcoholism and sobriety. This tally celebrating a whole decade sober is a stark, powerful tribute to what the singer-songwriter has overcome. Monica Schipper, Getty Images Morgan Wade's Passion for Ink She's one of country music's most heavily-tattooed young artists, but don't ask for the deep, personal meanings behind her ink. In a 2022 tweet , Wade wrote, "'Why did you get that tattoo?' Because. I. Felt. Like. It." Bryan Steffy, Getty Images Maren Morris' Souvenir for a Special Song Morris has a couple of eye-catching tattoos, but perhaps the sweetest is the hummingbird on her wrist. She has a song called "Hummingbird," which she wrote the day she found out she was pregnant with her son Hayes, making it easy to wonder if this tat is a tribute to him. Instagram Kelsea Ballerini's Mountains (With a View) A delicate little mountain range popped up on Kelsea Ballerini's forearm towards the end of her Heartfirst Tour in 2023. She hasn't explained the exact inspiration behind the tattoo, but her Rolling Up the Welcome Mat features a track called "Mountain With a View," and the song was a staple of her setlist in 2023. Kevin Winter, Getty Images Luke Bryan's Legendary Booty Tat Fans haven't seen Luke Bryan's butt tattoo in person, of course, but the singer has admitted to its existence. In an interview with Extra , Bryan said he's got his wife Caroline's initials inked on his derriere — and she's got his inked on hers. Kane Brown's Bad-A-- Gorilla Brown's incredible, realistic gorilla tattoo was inked by Inkmaster 's Season 9 champ, Bubba Irwin — but that's not all. The singer's friend and fellow country star Jason Aldean — who has also been tattooed by Irwin — etched one of the lines on Brown's arm while he was getting this tattoo. Monica Schipper, Getty Images Ronnie Dunn's Eye-Catching Statement Piece In case you're ever wondering whether or not Ronnie Dunn — one half of Brooks & Dunn — is a cowboy, all you've gotta do is check is forearm for confirmation. The word is inked there in huge, bold lettering. Legend has it , neither Dunn's wife nor his frequent tourmate Reba McEntire is a huge fan of the tattoo. Kevin Winter, Getty Images Tim McGraw's Ichthys McGraw's religious beliefs are the inspiration behind a couple of his tattoos, but this ichthys — also known as a "Jesus fish" on his bicep is the most eye-catching. Jason Kempin, Getty Images Tyler Hubbard's Majestic Travel Tat Hubbard got the idea for his large, intricately-design elephant tattoo during one of his trips to Africa. "They're just so majestic and honestly, it's also just a reminder to preserve and take care of our environment and our world and kind of that side of things," Hubbard told PopCulture about the tat . Tracy Lawrence's Mount Rushmore of Country Greats Lawrence's massive Mount Rushmore tattoo is a hat-tip to his four all-time favorite country stars: George Jones, George Strait, Keith Whitley and Merle Haggard. Now that's a solid lineup!
